en: José Rizal wrote the novels Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo to expose Spanish colonial abuses in the Philippines.
General Emilio Aguinaldo declared Philippine independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, in Kawit, Cavite.
The Legislative branch of the Philippine government is composed of the Senate and the House of Representatives.
The Philippine eagle, known locally as the monkey-eating eagle, is the national bird and an endangered species.
The sampaguita, a fragrant white flower, was officially declared the national flower of the Philippines in 1934.
The Ifugao people built the famous Banaue Rice Terraces in the Cordillera mountains over two thousand years ago.
The Philippines has over 180 distinct languages, with Tagalog, Cebuano, and Ilocano being among the most widely spoken.
Dr. Fe del Mundo was the first Asian woman admitted to Harvard Medical School and invented a bamboo incubator.
The Sinulog festival in Cebu honors the Santo Niño with a two-step forward, one-step backward dance ritual.
Filipino citizens acquire the right and duty to vote in national elections once they reach eighteen years old.
The South Sea pearl, harvested from the Pinctada maxima oyster, is officially recognized as the national gem of the Philippines.
The traditional Filipino value of bayanihan is shown when community members work together to carry a nipa hut.
